story.head: Oleksiak returns to Seattle
paras: The Canucks are on a seven-game losing streak, and the Kraken (9-7-1) lost 4-1 to Carolina on Nov 12. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Kraken fourth in the Pacific (22nd in the NHL).

The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.167) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .335, and their goaltending has held them back. The Kraken’s record (.559) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.436), largely thanks to their finishing.
In their seven-game skid, the Canucks have been outscored 30-14, including 18-9 at 5-on-5.

The Canucks have had shaky goaltending (32nd), have a leaky penalty kill (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). Vancouver has allowed 4.52 goals a game, the most in the league. As for the Kraken, they roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st) and rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd). They also keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st), so the Kraken keep dangerous shots away, but the Canucks give up a lot of them. Seattle has allowed 3.59 goals a game, the fourth most in the league.

Elias Pettersson (#40) (5 G / 16 A / 21 P in 21 GP) leads the Canucks in scoring, and Brock Boeser (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 21 GP) has a team-high seven goals. For the Kraken, Berkly Catton (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Frédérick Gaudreau (8 G / 3 A / 11 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eight goals.

Leevi Meriläinen (2-9-1 / .885 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Vancouver. Seattle has two options in net: Philipp Grubauer (5-4-1 / .887 SV% in 9 GS) and Joey Daccord (4-3-0 / .881 SV% in 8 GS). Grubauer has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Nov 12. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Lane Lambert likes to send Nyman, Meyers and Winterton out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against O'Connor, Sasson and Gallagher.

items.text: Jamie Oleksiak faces Seattle for the first time since leaving.
The Kraken have been without Jared McCann since Oct 22.
The Canucks have been without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.
Frédérick Gaudreau has seven goals on chances worth about 3.0 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
